bounds: One issuance request, one grant, two candidate credential identities with at most one persisted credential, two exchange attempts, two acknowledgement attempts, clock 0..3 measured from issuance, code deadline 1 and credential deadline 3. Attempts do not reuse slots.
fairness: Started requests settle under weak fairness of KMS and database completion. Success, request initiation and external authority recovery are not promised.
limitations: One issuance request, one grant, two candidate credential identities with at most one persisted credential, two exchange attempts, two acknowledgement attempts, clock 0..3 measured from issuance, code deadline 1 and credential deadline 3. Attempts do not reuse slots.
Client, redirect, environment, state and PKCE bytes are abstracted into matching or invalid input classes. Cryptographic algorithms and inference-policy authorities remain external assumptions.
The service captures a fresh confirmation timestamp after KMS, before awaiting SQL. Confirmation uses that captured value; transport delivery can occur after the code deadline.
Completed request-local timestamps and snapshots are cleared. Persistent grant, credential and reply identities remain in the state.
The credential model treats safe cleanup atomically. MobileAppGrantCleanup models planning and batch transactions separately; composition is not mechanically established.
Repeated failures beyond the two attempts, arbitrary database corruption, native durable storage and multi-grant authentication traffic remain outside the credential instance.
